attributes.body_ja:
「だけでなく」は「(A) 以外（いがい）にもある」と言（い）うときに使（つか）われる文法（ぶんぽう）です。この「だけでなく」を含（ふく）む文（ぶん）の後半（こうはん）に副助詞（ふくじょし）の「も」を付（つ）けると、(B) も (A) と同（おな）じカテゴリーのものであることをより強調（きょうちょう）する表現（ひょうげん）になります。

「だけ」そのものは副助詞（ふくじょし）で、主（おも）に名詞（めいし）のあとに置（お）かれます。そのあと、助動詞（じょどうし）「だ」の連用形（れんようけい）の否定形（ひていけい）が来（き）ます。

「て」は絶対（ぜったい）に必要（ひつよう）なわけではありませんが、これを付（つ）けることで、文（ぶん）の (A) と (B) をより自然（しぜん）に分（わ）けることができます。

「でなく」や「ではなく」を含（ふく）むほかの文法（ぶんぽう）と同（おな）じように、この文法（ぶんぽう）でも「じゃなく」や「じゃなくて」という形（かたち）を使（つか）うことができます。
attributes.body:
As an extension of the standard だけでなく, meaning 'not only, but also', adding the adverbial particle も to the (B) part of a sentence will place extra emphasis on the thing that is being included in the same category as (A).

だけ itself is an adverbial particle, so will primarily follow nouns. After this, the negative conjunctive form of the auxiliary verb だ (でなく) will create the 'not only' meaning.

て is not strictly required as part of this structure, but will help to create a far more natural 'separation' between (A) and (B) when it is used.

Either じゃなく or じゃなくて may also be used, as is the case with all でなく and ではなく based grammar structures.

attributes.description: Difference between でない and ではない
~だけでなく・～だけではなくて・～だけしゃなくて
だけでなくvs ばかりでなく vs はもちろん

attributes.body: ばかり emphasizes exclusivity, meaning 'only' or 'nothing but', e.g. 肉ばかり食べている ('He eats nothing but meat'). だけでなく～も expresses inclusion, meaning 'not only…but also', e.g. 肉だけでなく野菜も食べている ('He eats not only meat but also vegetables'). Compared to だけ, ばかり often carries a stronger nuance of excess or doing something too much.

second_relatable.title: だけでなく(て)～も
second_relatable.meaning: Not only ~ but ~ also, Not just ~ but ~ also

attributes.body: をはじめ gives a representative example and implies that others follow, e.g. 東京をはじめ、全国でイベントが行われた ('The event was held across the country, starting with Tokyo'). だけでなく(て)～も lists multiple elements without suggesting one is more representative, e.g. 東京だけでなく大阪でも人気だ ('It's popular not only in Tokyo but also in Osaka').

second_relatable.title: だけでなく(て)～も
second_relatable.meaning: Not only ~ but ~ also, Not just ~ but ~ also

attributes.body: ばかりでなく and だけでなく(て)～も are nearly identical in meaning, both meaning 'Not only (A), but also (B)'. ばかりでなく is the more formal expression, while だけでなく (especially in the alternate form だけじゃなくて) is more common in everyday speech. For example, 日本語ばかりでなく、韓国語も話せる 'He can speak not only Japanese, but also Korean.' vs. 日本語だけじゃなくて、韓国語も話せる (Same meaning, but more casual in tone).

attributes.body: のみならず and だけでなく(て)～も are nearly identical in meaning, both meaning 'Not only (A), but also (B)'. のみならず is by far the more formal expression, while だけでなく (especially in the alternate form だけじゃなくて) is more common in everyday speech. For example, 日本語のみならず、韓国語も話せる 'He can speak not only Japanese, but also Korean.' vs. 日本語だけじゃなくて、韓国語も話せる (Same meaning, but far more casual).

second_relatable.title: だけでなく(て)～も
second_relatable.meaning: Not only ~ but ~ also, Not just ~ but ~ also

attributes.body: Both express that something applies to more than one item, but differ in nuance and tone. だけでなく(て)～も is a neutral 'Not only (A), but also (B)', e.g. 日本語だけでなく、韓国語も話せる 'He can speak not only Japanese, but also Korean.' はもとより is more literary and formal, and suggests the first item is obvious, e.g. 親はもとより先生にも感謝しています 'I'm grateful not only to my parents, but also to my teachers.'

first_relatable.title: はもとより
first_relatable.meaning: Not only... but also, Let alone, Of course

second_relatable.title: だけでなく(て)～も
second_relatable.meaning: Not only ~ but ~ also, Not just ~ but ~ also

attributes.body: Both express 'not only (A), but also (B)', but the nuance differs. はもちろん stresses (A) as obvious, e.g. 寿司はもちろん納豆も食べる ('He eats not only sushi, but also natto'). だけでなく gives equal weight to both, e.g. 映画だけでなくドラマも好きだ ('I like not only movies, but also TV dramas').

attributes.body: だけでなく (or だけでなくて, だけじゃなくて, etc.) is a common expression that means 'not only'. It is often followed by another noun + も in the expression だけでなく(て)～も, which has the meaning of 'not only (A), but also (B)', e.g. 肉だけでなく、魚も食べる ('I eat not only meat, but also fish.'). In other words, だけでなく(て)～も is an extension of the だけでなく pattern when you want to specify the additional thing or quality.
